name: Black-throated Shrike-Tanager
rangeDescription: Gulf-caribbean lowlands of southeastern mexico to northwestern honduras
description: Uncommon inhabitant of humid evergreen forest in tropical lowlands. Found singly or in pairs, typically perched quietly and rather upright at middle to upper levels inside the forest.

name: Ochre-headed Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A small flycatcher. Male is glossy blue-black with a white belly and base of the undertail.

name: Green-backed Trogon
rangeDescription: East of the andes from colombia southward to peru and bolivia, and eastward to trinidad, the guianas, and eastern brazil (to maranhão and mato grosso; also alagoas, and from bahia southward to são paulo
description: Often first detected by its song: a melodic series of “kua kua kua kua” notes, similar to Surucua Trogon, but faster. Perches quietly in an upright position for long periods.

name: Flesh-footed Shearwater
rangeDescription: Southern indian and southwestern pacific oceans; winters to arabian sea and northwestern pacific
description: Entirely the color of dark chocolate with a dark-tipped pink bill. Fairly large; similar in size and shape to Pink-footed Shearwater.

name: Sage Thrasher
rangeDescription: Arid southern british columbia to baja california and central mexico
description: The smallest thrasher; crisp black streaking on underparts unlike most other western thrashers. Grayish brown with buffy wash on belly and sides and thin white wingbars.

name: Samoan Island-Thrush
rangeDescription: Samoa (savai'i and upolu)
description: Dark thrush with orange bill, eyering, legs, and feet. Endemic to Samoa, where found only at the highest elevations and generally not often encountered.

name: Dusky White-eye
rangeDescription: Woodland of palau archipelago (western caroline islands)
description: Small and rather drab. Brown above, darkest on head and wings.

name: Makira Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A tiny warbler with a mostly gray head, a dark eye-stripe, and a pale eyebrow. Back and wings strongly green-toned with two buff wingbars.

name: Antioquia Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Central andes of northern colombia (antioquia and eastern caldas)
description: Rare flycatcher known only from a few sites in the Colombian Andes, mainly in the northern part of the central range. It is fairly small and mostly yellow, with a gray crown and broad, yellow wingbars.

name: Australasian Gannet
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off southeastern australia including tasmania, and coasts and islands off new zealand
description: Large black-and-white seabird with heavy, pointed bill. Adult white with black flight feathers and central tail feathers, yellow-washed head.

name: Spot-breasted Lapwing
rangeDescription: Montane grassland of ethiopia
description: A chunky lapwing of the Ethiopian highlands. Note the black cap, white eyebrow, black throat, and coarse spots across the breast.

name: White-spotted Munia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern new guinea (lorentz river eastward at least to the kikori river region, and perhaps farther eastward)
description: A small brown bird with a heavy blue bill, rufous underparts, and white spotting across the head, back, and breast. The pale buff rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Plumbeous Warbler
rangeDescription: Guadeloupe including terre-de-haut and marie-galante (just to south of guadeloupe) and dominica (central lesser antilles)
description: A striking small bird that frequents montane forests, but sometimes ventures into dry scrub and mangroves. This species is readily distinguished by its overall gray plumage (tinged green above and yellow below on immature birds) with boldly contrasting white eyebrows and wingbars.

name: Flock Bronzewing
rangeDescription: Northwestern australia to western queensland and northwestern new south wales
description: Large desert pigeon, typically observed as fast-flying flocks coming in to drink in the morning or evening in arid and semi-arid inland Northern Australia. Plain brown above, plain gray below.

name: Lesser Spotted Eagle
rangeDescription: Locally in eastern europe to caspian lowlands; winters to southern africa
description: Medium-sized, compact eagle. Adults are conspicuously two toned when perched: dark flight feathers contrast with paler body.

name: Boulder Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of far southern peru (puno) to northern bolivia and northwestern argentina
description: Gray finch-like bird with an oddly elongated bill. It is only found in boulder fields and other rocky areas of the high Andes, usually above treeline.

name: Narrow-billed Antwren
rangeDescription: Interior eastern brazil (eastern bahia and northeastern minas gerais)
description: Long-tailed antwren with white flanks, unmistakable within its restricted range. Males are dark gray with a black bib.

name: Wood Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds northern eurasia; winters to southern africa, southern asia, and australia
description: Medium-sized brownish wader with a white belly, varied pale spotting and spangling on back. In flight shows plain upperwings, square white rump patch.

name: Southern Grosbeak-Canary
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A large seedeater with a very thick pinkish bill. Brownish-olive above and yellow below with streaking along the sides.
imageCreditName: Keith Valentine I Rockjumper Birding Tours

name: Dideric Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Intra-african migrant in sub-saharan africa and southern arabia
description: A small, greenish cuckoo. The male has barred flanks, white flecking on the wing, white patches in front of and behind the eye, and a distinctly red eye surrounded by a red eye-ring.
